audit.whatIsWrong: Five of seven rows disagreed with the already-audited mirror, and two of them gave the late game to Gnar while every piece of prose on the page says you out-scale him hard.
audit.why: The mirror audit on gnar__vladimir settled this chart as Gnar, Gnar, Skill, Gnar, Skill, Vladimir, Vladimir and applied it across both its layers. That shape also fits 54.72% — Gnar bullies the early levels, you take over once items land. Leaving first-item and 2+ items on Gnar contradicted whys[5], whys[6] and the entire late paragraph.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 2, 3, 5 and 6 flipped as matched win[N] + phases[N].side pairs with ratings rescaled, landing exactly on the mirror's chart.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page tracks 'GNAR!' as the matchup-defining cooldown without ever saying what it costs him.
audit.why: GNAR! is 90/60/30 seconds — at rank 1 it is a once-a-lane commitment, by rank 3 it is up almost every fight, which changes how long a bait is worth. Your Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 and his Wallop stun is a flat 7s in Mega form.
audit.corrected: Real cooldowns written into report[5].t and spikes[1].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions never reached the page: Sanguine Pool's 2 seconds of untargetability eats the GNAR! knockup-stun and Wallop outright, and Tides of Blood is blocked by enemy units so poking through the wave does nothing.
audit.why: Riot's text: Sanguine Pool 'becoming untargetable for 2 seconds'; Tides 'can be blocked by enemy units'. Against a champion whose whole kill plan is one Mega engage, the untargetable window is the matchup, and the unit-block explains why the poke war feels lost through a big wave.
audit.corrected: Written into spikes[0].text, spikes[1].text and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[0].d told you to track GNAR! without naming the actual tell.
audit.why: The Rage bar is the tell: at maximum Rage his next ability transforms him, so the read is the bar, not the cast.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d now names the Rage bar.

edits.before: At level 3 his Q-into-W combo out-trades your single-target Q while your pool is down.
edits.after: Level 3 is even: bait Boomerang Throw, then trade while its 13s cooldown runs.

edits.before: At 6 you spike first: Hemoplague plus E stacks lets you all-in his Mini form.
edits.after: At 6 it is even — Hemoplague amps, but Mega's stun still answers your all-in.

edits.before: Mini Gnar bullies you with Boomerang Throw (Q) plus the Hyper (W) auto-attack stacks that proc a burst of bonus damage every third hit, out-trading your single-target Transfusion (Q) whenever your pool is empty.
edits.after: Mini Gnar bullies you with Boomerang Throw (Q) at 1100 range plus Hyper (W) stacks that burst every third auto. Tides of Blood is blocked by enemy units, so poke him from an open angle and never through the middle of the wave.

edits.before: You hit your real power spike first — Hemoplague (R) plus stacked Tides of Blood (E) lets you all-in when Gnar is still in Mini form, and if he rages you can Sanguine Pool (W) under his GNAR! (R) knockback to survive it.
edits.after: You spike first: Hemoplague (R) plus stacked Tides of Blood (E) lets you all-in while Gnar is still Mini. If he rages, Sanguine Pool's 2 seconds of untargetable eats GNAR! (R) and the Wallop stun outright — but the pool is 28s, so spend it on nothing else.

edits.before: Track Gnar's GNAR! (Mega Stun): His Mega all-in. Pool after it. When it is down — Q-E + R him.
edits.after: GNAR! (R) is 90s at rank 1 but only 30s at rank 3 — pool the wall-stun, then Q-E-R him.

edits.before: His Mega all-in. Pool after it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Rage bar full means Mega on his next cast — step back before he flips.

notes: The packet chart (Gnar x4 then Vladimir x3) and the mirror chart differ at rows 2 and 4. I followed the mirror, which is already applied on gnar__vladimir, so the two directions agree; the difference is one shared row either way and not a power claim.
